prompt.context_jp: 病院の廊下に、比奈を呼び止める深沢の声____響いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 病院の廊下に、比奈を呼び止める深沢の声____響いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits best.

feedback.correct_en: The scene opens by introducing a new sound into the setting — Fukazawa's voice. New information entering a scene like this takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark the voice as an already-established topic, which doesn't fit a fresh scene-opener. を would ungrammatically treat 声 as an object of 響いた (an intransitive verb).

contrast_examples.en: A voice echoed in the corridor. (new event)

contrast_examples.jp: その声は今も忘れられない。
contrast_examples.en: That voice — I still can't forget it. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 同じ頃、大学校舎の一室では、爆発に巻き込まれた講師の中里の呼吸____浅くなっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 講師の中里の呼吸____浅くなっていた。

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is reporting a new developing situation inside this scene — Nakazato's breathing is becoming shallow. Fresh reportive information takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame 呼吸 as an already-known topic being commented on, but here it's new descriptive detail of an unfolding emergency.

contrast_examples.jp: 患者の呼吸が浅くなった。
中里の呼吸は、もう正常だ。

prompt.context_jp: 処置に必要な器材は乏しく、届いた点滴だけ____命綱だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 届いた点滴だけ____命綱だった。

feedback.correct_en: The structure 〜だけが emphasizes exclusivity — the IV drip, and only it, is the lifeline. が with だけ gives exhaustive focus.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは is possible in other contexts but would shift the nuance to 'at least the IV' as a topic; here the writer identifies the single lifeline, which fits が.

contrast_examples.jp: それだけは言わないで。

prompt.context_jp: 時計の針____、犯人の指定した時刻へと確実に進んでいく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 時計の針____、犯人の指定した時刻へと確実に進んでいく。

feedback.correct_en: The clock hands are being set up as the topic the sentence will comment on — a general, continuing state. は frames the topic for narration.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal that the clock hands are new information just appearing in the scene, but here they are already visible to everyone — the narrator is commenting about them.

contrast_examples.jp: 時計の針は進んでいく。
contrast_examples.en: The clock hands keep moving (as everyone watches).
The clock hands stopped! (surprising new fact)

prompt.context_jp: 「犯人の内通者____いるかぎり 動けない」
prompt.prompt_jp: 犯人の内通者____いるかぎり 動けない

feedback.correct_en: 〜がいる asserts the existence of an informant — new, consequential information that justifies not moving. Existential clauses in subordinate 'as long as' take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 内通者は would make 'the informant' a known topic, but the point here is the existence itself (there IS a mole inside), which demands が.

contrast_examples.jp: 反対する人がいるかぎり、進められない。
contrast_examples.en: As long as there are opponents, we can't proceed.

contrast_examples.jp: その内通者は捕まった。

prompt.context_jp: 「格好のスケープゴート____いて 助かったわ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 格好のスケープゴート____いて 助かったわ

feedback.correct_en: The bureaucrat is relieved that a scapegoat exists — pure existential/new-information が. The speaker is identifying who is available to take the blame.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly treat 'a convenient scapegoat' as pre-established topic; the sentiment here is 'there happens to be one, lucky us.'

contrast_examples.jp: いい人がいて助かった。
contrast_examples.en: Lucky there was a good person around.

prompt.context_jp: 時間だけ____、無情に削られていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 時間だけ____、無情に削られていった。

feedback.correct_en: だけが highlights 'time, and nothing else' was being whittled away — the exhaustive-focus pattern. Nothing is progressing except the countdown.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would suggest 'at least time' as a contrastive topic ('time, at any rate...'), which doesn't match the despairing tone that time ALONE is moving.

contrast_examples.jp: 時間だけが過ぎていく。

contrast_examples.en: Just for today, I want to rest.

prompt.context_jp: 「私____ 目の前の命を 救いたいだけです 椿さんは関係ありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私____ 目の前の命を 救いたいだけです

feedback.correct_en: Kitami is distancing himself from Tsubaki — 'As for ME (unlike him), I only want to save lives.' This contrastive self-topic is classic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私が would sound like he's identifying himself as the one who wants to save lives (answering 'who?'), but no such question is on the table. The tone here is contrastive, not identificational.

contrast_examples.en: I (for my part) am against it.
I'll be the one to do it. (volunteering)

prompt.context_jp: 閉ざされていた記憶の扉____、ゆっくりと開き始める。
prompt.prompt_jp: 閉ざされていた記憶の扉____、ゆっくりと開き始める。

feedback.correct_en: A new narrative event — the door of memory beginning to open — is being introduced descriptively. Fresh scene-reporting takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 'the door of memory' into an ongoing topic, but the sentence is marking the moment the opening begins, not commenting about a known door.

contrast_examples.jp: その扉は、もう二度と開かない。
contrast_examples.en: That door will never open again. (comment on topic)

prompt.context_jp: 椿の口ぶり____親しげで、涼香の警戒を巧みに解いていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 椿の口ぶり____親しげで、涼香の警戒を巧みに解いていった。

feedback.correct_en: The narrator sets Tsubaki's manner of speaking as the topic and then characterizes it (親しげ) and its effect. は is the natural topic marker for this kind of character description.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it sound like 'Tsubaki's tone' is being newly identified against alternatives, but it's simply the subject under discussion as the narrator describes him.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の話し方は穏やかだ。
contrast_examples.en: His way of speaking is calm. (description)
It's his way of speaking that bothers me. (focus)

prompt.context_jp: 画面には、妹の名____浮かんでいる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 画面には、妹の名____浮かんでいる。

feedback.correct_en: Kitami notices something new on the screen — his sister's name. New information appearing in a scene is marked with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 'his sister's name' as a known topic being commented on; but the whole point is that he suddenly notices it there.

contrast_examples.en: A name appeared on the screen. (noticed)

prompt.context_jp: 「私なんです 椿さんと つながっていたの____」
prompt.prompt_jp: 椿さんと つながっていたの____ 私なんです

feedback.correct_en: The structure here presupposes 'the one who was connected to Tsubaki' as the topic, and identifies 私 as that person. The nominalized clause takes は, with 私 as the exhaustive-focus answer.
feedback.incorrect_en: つながっていたのが私です is possible in cleft form, but the given word order (私なんです ... のは) requires は on the presupposed element.

contrast_examples.en: The one who did it is me.

prompt.context_jp: 大杉の顔から、急速に色____失われていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 大杉の顔から、急速に色____失われていった。

feedback.correct_en: The narrator reports an unfolding change — color draining from the face. New, dramatic reportive content takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 色は would make 'color' a known topic being contrasted, but this is a sudden observed event, not a topic comment.

contrast_examples.jp: 顔から血の気が引いた。
あの子の顔色は、いつも悪い。
contrast_examples.en: That child's complexion is always bad. (habitual topic)

prompt.context_jp: 「私たち____応援されたくて やってるわけではないので」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私たち____応援されたくて やってるわけではないので

feedback.correct_en: Otowa frames her team as the topic and distances them from doing this for praise. は carries the contrastive 'as for us, that's not why' nuance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私たちが would answer 'who is doing it?', which isn't the question — she's declaring the team's stance against the superior's claim about criticism.

contrast_examples.jp: 私たちは、ただ命を救いたいだけです。
contrast_examples.en: We just want to save lives.
We'll be the ones to do it. (volunteering)

prompt.context_jp: モニターの音____、突如、警告音へと変わった。
prompt.prompt_jp: モニターの音____、突如、警告音へと変わった。

feedback.correct_en: A sudden event changes the situation — the monitor's sound shifting to an alarm. Sudden perceptual changes in narration take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 音は would frame 'the sound' as the pre-existing topic being described in general; but the point is the abrupt change, which demands が.

contrast_examples.jp: 急にアラーム音が鳴った。
モニターの音は小さい。
contrast_examples.en: The monitor sound is quiet. (general description)

prompt.context_jp: モニターの波形____、無情な直線を描いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: モニターの波形____、無情な直線を描いた。

feedback.correct_en: A dramatic new event — the waveform flatlining. Narrative scene-reports of what happens next take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 波形は would be a general comment about the waveform; but here it's a single, devastating moment, so が carries the shock.

contrast_examples.jp: 波形はまだ安定している。
contrast_examples.en: The waveform is still stable. (ongoing state)

prompt.context_jp: 一対の若い医師の間に、隠しきれない緊張が____いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一対の若い医師の間に、隠しきれない緊張が____いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that collocates with 緊張.

feedback.correct_en: 緊張が漂う ('tension hangs in the air') is the fixed collocation for atmospheric tension between people.
feedback.incorrect_en: 流れる is used for time or liquids, and 落ちる doesn't collocate with 緊張 at all. Only 漂う captures the sense of tension floating in the space.

contrast_examples.en: A heavy atmosphere hangs over us.

prompt.context_jp: 誰もが____詰めて、その一秒を数えていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 誰もが____詰めて、その一秒を数えていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that fits this set expression.

feedback.correct_en: 息を詰める is a fixed expression meaning 'hold one's breath in tense anticipation,' which fits the countdown perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: 胸を詰める isn't a standard idiom; 胸が詰まる (be choked up) exists but with 詰まる, not 詰める. 喉を詰める refers to physical choking, not emotional tension.

prompt.context_jp: 喜多見は湧き上がる憤りを____きれず、拳を固く握った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 喜多見は湧き上がる憤りを____きれず、拳を固く握った。

feedback.correct_en: 憤りを抑える ('suppress anger') is the standard collocation for restraining an inner emotion. 抑えきれず means 'unable to hold back.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 止める is used for external motion or activity, not surging emotion. 隠す is 'hide,' which works grammatically but doesn't fit the image of fists clenching from unleashed rage.

prompt.context_jp: 南の詰問に、喜多見は一度深く息を____。
prompt.prompt_jp: 喜多見は一度深く息を____。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that collocates with 息.

feedback.correct_en: 深く息を吸う ('take a deep breath') is the natural collocation for composing oneself before speaking.
feedback.incorrect_en: 息を引く isn't used in modern Japanese. 息を抜く means 'take a breather / relax,' which doesn't fit the tense interrogation context.

contrast_examples.jp: 深呼吸をして落ち着く。
contrast_examples.en: Take a deep breath and calm down.

prompt.context_jp: 椿の口ぶりは親しげで、涼香の警戒を巧みに____いった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 涼香の警戒を巧みに____いった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that collocates with 警戒.

feedback.correct_en: 警戒を解く ('let one's guard down / disarm wariness') is the fixed verb pair for easing someone's caution.
feedback.incorrect_en: 開く is used for doors/eyes/meetings, not inner states. 外す can be used for restraints but not for 警戒 as a mental state.

prompt.context_jp: 奪われまいとする手が、器具の柄を____しめる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 器具の柄を____しめる。

feedback.correct_en: 握りしめる ('clench, grip tightly') is the compound verb for seizing something like a handle with a fist. The 〜しめる suffix pairs most naturally with 握る.
feedback.incorrect_en: 抱きしめる means 'embrace tightly' (a person). 掴みしめる is not a standard compound verb; 掴む alone would work, but not with 〜しめる.

prompt.context_jp: その言葉には、____色はまったくなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: その言葉には、____色はまったくなかった。

feedback.correct_en: 責める means 'to blame/reproach' and fits the context where Kitami speaks without a hint of blame toward the student who confessed. 責める色 = a tone of blame.
feedback.incorrect_en: 攻める means 'attack' (military/sports). 怒る can't modify a noun this way (怒る色 isn't idiomatic; it would be 怒りの色).

contrast_examples.jp: 彼を責めるつもりはない。
contrast_examples.en: I don't mean to blame him.

prompt.context_jp: 涼香がふと切り出した口ぶりに、幸太は思わず____。
prompt.prompt_jp: 幸太は思わず____。

feedback.correct_en: 身構える ('brace oneself, go on guard') captures Kota's reflexive tensing-up when his sister's tone shifts to something serious.
feedback.incorrect_en: 振り向く is physical turning around, 見つめる is 'stare at.' Neither captures the inner bracing against anticipated news that fits the context.

contrast_examples.en: Brace oneself upon hearing the news.

prompt.context_jp: Kitami defends himself against the accusation that he is in league with Tsubaki.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for Kitami's defense in this interrogation?

choices.text: 私は目の前の命を救いたいだけです。椿さんは関係ありません。
私が目の前の命を救いたいだけです。椿さんが関係ありません。
私は目の前の命が救いたいだけです。椿さんは関係ないです。

feedback.correct_en: Version A uses は on 私 (contrastive self-topic: 'as for me') and 椿さんは関係ありません (negated topic), which is exactly how a speaker denies involvement.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's double が sounds like exhaustive identification ('I am the one who wants to save'), unnatural here. C mixes が on 命 — 救いたい can take を or が, but mid-sentence の is cleaner — and 関係ないです is slightly less formal in this setting.

contrast_examples.en: I have nothing to do with it.

contrast_examples.jp: 私が関係ないわけがない。

prompt.context_jp: Kitami rallies the students despite the public criticism against him.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as an impassioned appeal?

choices.text: どんな批判をされてもかまいません。だけど、命を救うことには手を貸してほしい！
どんな批判がされてもかまいません。だけど、命を救うことに手が貸してほしい！
どんな批判をしてもかまいません。だけど、命を救うことで手を貸してほしい！

feedback.correct_en: A uses the passive 批判をされる correctly and the fixed phrase 手を貸す ('lend a hand'). The には focuses the request on this particular task.
feedback.incorrect_en: B swaps を→が incorrectly in both clauses, breaking the passive and the idiom. C changes the voice (される→する) so 'however much I criticize' — wrong meaning — and で instead of に misroutes the help.

contrast_examples.jp: 批判をされる覚悟はある。

prompt.context_jp: Kitami explains to the patient why he promises absolutes even though doctors are taught not to.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for Kitami's gentle explanation?

choices.text: そう言うとね、患者さんだけじゃなくて、俺自身も勇気づけられるんですよ。
そう言うとね、患者さんだけじゃなくて、俺自身を勇気づけられるんですよ。
そう言ったら、患者さんだけじゃなくて、俺自身が勇気づけるんですよ。

feedback.correct_en: A uses the passive 勇気づけられる with も to say 'I too am given courage.' This matches Kitami's reflective tone to the patient.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses を with the passive, which is ungrammatical. C changes to active 勇気づける (I give courage to myself) and loses the reflexive-passive nuance that makes the line heartfelt.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の言葉に勇気づけられた。
contrast_examples.en: I was encouraged by his words.

prompt.context_jp: Kitami reassures Osugi after her tearful confession.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as reassurance?

choices.text: あなたなら、やり直せます。絶対に。
あなただと、やり直せます。絶対に。
あなたは、やり直させます。絶対に。

feedback.correct_en: あなたなら ('if it's you,' 'in your case') carries confident encouragement — 'you, of all people, can start over.' This is the standard inspirational pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's あなただと sounds conditional in a factual/descriptive way ('when it's you'), which lacks the warm encouragement. C's causative やり直させる means 'make start over,' misassigning agency.

contrast_examples.jp: あなただと時間がかかる。
contrast_examples.en: With you (as the agent), it takes time. (descriptive)

prompt.context_jp: Minami's gruff response to Kitami's thanks, keeping emotional distance.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for Minami's cold, formal line?

choices.text: 国民の命を守るのが俺の仕事だ。お前を信用したわけじゃない。
国民の命は守るのが俺の仕事だ。お前は信用したわけじゃない。
国民の命を守るが俺の仕事だ。お前を信用したわけじゃないよ。

feedback.correct_en: A uses the cleft 〜のが…だ to identify Minami's job, and お前を信用した with を is the correct object-marking. The blunt sentence-final だ matches his stern register.
feedback.incorrect_en: B puts は on 命 and お前, weakening the cleft identification and giving an odd contrastive feel. C drops the nominalizer の from 守るのが (ungrammatical) and softens the end with よ, which doesn't fit his cold tone.

contrast_examples.jp: お前を信じたんじゃない。
contrast_examples.en: It's not that I trusted you.
